idea: Why a toilet may keep running
title: Diagnosing a Continuously Running Toilet
description: A toilet that runs continuously wastes hundreds of liters of water daily. The most frequent cause is a faulty flapper valve at the bottom of the tank. Over time, mineral deposits or chlorine deterioration prevent the flexible rubber flapper from forming a watertight seal against the flush valve seat. This allows water to constantly seep into the bowl, triggering the fill valve to run continuously to maintain tank water levels. Inspecting the flapper for rigidity, warped edges, or mineral buildup is the essential first step. Replacing a degraded flapper restores the seal and stops water loss immediately. visual_story: The visual provides a clear internal sectional view of a toilet tank, directing focus directly to the flapper valve at the flush valve opening. Viewers immediately see how the rubber flapper acts as the primary seal holding water in the tank, demonstrating why material breakdown at this exact contact point allows water to escape continuously into the bowl.

on_image_text.explanation: A worn or distorted flapper fails to seal against the flush valve seat, letting water escape into the bowl.
on_image_text.takeaway: Inspect the rubber flapper for stiffness or warping before replacing the entire fill mechanism.
